alignments.note: Inflected verb takes its supplied subject pronoun; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb.
Dative pronoun with its case preposition.
Rule 65: the conditional particle of a concessive εἰ καί takes the English word introducing the clause, here *Though*.
Rule 65: the intensifying καί is decided on its own, and the ASV writes no word for it here.
Ordinary negative aligned to *not*.

Rule 88: the ASV converts the participle ἀναστάς into a coordinate finite clause, so the supplied juncture *and* is a helper on the finite verb it introduces; the subject and auxiliary ride along under rule 9 and the discontinuity is licensed by rule 15.
Dative object pronoun.
Participle rendered as a bare coordinate verb; the *and* belongs to δώσει under rule 88.
Rule 61: the preposition governing an articular infinitive takes the English clause-introducer, here *because*.
Rule 61: the nominalizing article of an articular infinitive has no English realization.
The infinitive is expanded into a finite clause; its supplied subject is a rule 7 helper on the verb itself (rule 74).
Predicate noun standing bare, the possessive belonging to αὐτοῦ.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive *his*.
The complex preposition *because of* is one rendering of διά and is not split; rule 21 forbids leaving a bare *of* on the article, which is displaced here in any case.
Emphatic particle realized by *yet*.
Rule 20: the genitive pronoun αὐτοῦ takes the possessive *his*, so the article realizes nothing.
Noun rendered *importunity*.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive *his*.
Participle rendered as a bare coordinate verb, the *and* belonging to the finite δώσει under rule 88.
As with s006: subject, auxiliary and the supplied juncture *and* ride with the finite verb under rules 9 and 88, discontinuously under rule 15.
Dative object pronoun.

Correlative quantity relative rendered by the frame *as many as*; rule 104 heads such a unit on the dimension word, as ὅσαι → *how many soever be* heads on *many*. The marginal *whatsoever things* is not the text rendered.
Inflected verb with its supplied subject pronoun, headed on the lexical verb under rule 9.

review_notes: εἰ καί is split under rule 65 rather than treated as one concessive unit; καί is left unrepresented because the ASV writes no word for it.
Both finite δώσει units carry the supplied *and* under rule 88, leaving each participle a bare verb; giving the *and* to the participle it follows was rejected as the single contrary corpus reading.
Variant v005 leaves φίλον αὐτοῦ as in the base projection, which the ASV's *his friend* matches; v006 is selected base and needs no further decision.
